hypotheses.justification: `Refines n q p` (Progress.lean l.41) only looks at `q.cst`. By `individualize_cst_eq` (Equivariance.lean l.523, proved by `rfl`), `(individualize p v).1.cst` depends on `v` only through `p.pos[v]!`: it is `setCstFrom c ec (ec - (c+1)) (c+1) p.cst` with `c = p.cst[p.pos[v]!]!` and `ec = p.cen[p.pos[v]!]!`. Proof without `hv`: if `v < n`, use the current proof. Otherwise `v ≥ n`. If `n = 0`, `Refines 0 _ _` holds trivially because no `i < 0` exists. If `n > 0`, `hp.posSize` gives `p.pos.size = n ≤ v`, so `p.pos[v]! = default = 0` (by `getElem!_neg`). Take `w := p.lab[0]!`. Then `hp.labLt 0` gives `w < n` and `hp.posLab 0` gives `p.pos[w]! = 0`. Rewriting with `individualize_cst_eq` therefore gives `(individualize p v).1.cst = (individualize p w).1.cst`, and the existing proof applies to `w` since `w < n`. So the statement stays true and provable without `hv`. `hp` is still needed. Counterexample without it: `n = 3`, `cst = [0,1,2]`, `cen = [3,3,3]`, `pos[0] = 0`. Individualising vertex 0 sets the new `cst[2]` to `1`, so cell start 2 is lost.
